Fix verified: the added relative clause "that followed them" resolves "them" anaphorically to the immediately preceding list ("the setup posts, the plan-file templates, the verifier write-ups") inside the SAME clause — this is now ordinary intra-sentence anaphora, not a pointer to something unestablished. A cold reader parses it as "reversals of those posts/templates/write-ups," a generic category claim about the field's written record, not a specific-but-unnamed event. Harm no longer present; PASS. Fresh full-deck read found no other never-named / vague-with-history / stranded-by-rechunk referents: chunk 0's "the packaged re-send" and chunk 1's "the diagnose-and-re-send you just ran" (line 200) resolve via the module-arc-beats-in-openers/closers carve-out (this lecture is included directly after `diagnose-and-resend.md` in `learn-from-the-test.md`); chunk 2's "Ralph" (line 212, plan.md bullet) resolves to "Geoffrey Huntley's Ralph" named two sentences earlier in the SAME chunk (line 210); chunk 6's "the kit" (line 235) resolves to chunk 2's naming (line 210, "combined them into one kit and gave them names") per the arc-earned-vocabulary carve-out. Chunk 9 line 256 opens with "The loop" (first bare mention of this exact phrase in-file) — checked against two carve-outs and both clear it: (a) arc-earned spine vocabulary — "the loop" is check_slides.md's OWN worked example of pre-earned training vocabulary, and it is genuinely earned well before M5 (grepped the corpus: `spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` (M1) and `agent-loop-raw.md` name and teach "the loop" long before this file); (b) the chunk's own header "Every re-feed pass starts a fresh session" (in-chunk per rule 1's own header clause) names the re-feed mechanism the bullet elaborates, and the exercise the student just ran (`diagnose-and-resend.md` Phase 3) offers "Ralph re-feed. Loop the prompt with a check baked in" as one of three verifier-shape menu options — so "the loop" also resolves as a module-arc/session-artifact callback regardless of the carve-out. The file's own maintainer block (line 262) shows this exact seam was deliberately engineered ("A judge reading *re-anchoring* in the exercise's Ralph re-feed bullet as a dangling referent should resolve it here") — accept-by-design, not a fresh finding.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Bold count per chunk, re-counted fresh against current line numbers: chunk1=1 ("A check is a position fix", line 200), chunk2=2 ("Reference artefact" line 211 / "plan.md" line 212), chunk3=1 ("External verifier", line 216), chunk4=1 ("candidates", line 225), chunk5=1 ("A prediction is not a measurement.", line 230), chunk6=1 ("The engineer decides", line 237), chunk7=1 ("hook", line 242), chunk8=1 ("Must happen goes in a hook", line 247), chunk9=0. All within the <=1-per-slide budget except chunk 2's pre-existing 2, which reads as the rule's own "consolidation slide may carry one handle per law" exception — two distinct named artefacts (Reference artefact, plan.md), each the sole bold in its own bullet. Chunk 5's "A prediction is not a measurement." is a whole six-word sentence bolded, which a literal read of "never a whole lead sentence" would catch on its own — but it is the sole bold on its slide, functions as one of a set of parallel epigrammatic laws this file coins as a device (siblings: chunk 1's "A check is a position fix", chunk 6's "The engineer decides"), and IS the governing claim of its bullet rather than a lead-in to elaboration below it — matching rule 9's "named laws" category. Harm check: the rule exists to stop every-bullet-bolded monoculture that dilutes which bold is a real handle; here exactly one law is bolded per slide against otherwise-plain prose, so the signal the rule protects stays intact. Not filing a REVISE.
